stem: What biophysical detail does this mean-field model retain that conventional neural mass models approximate away?
choices: Synaptic short-term plasticity between populations
Dendritic morphology of individual neurons
Axonal conduction delays within the population
Ion exchange between intracellular and extracellular space
answer: Ion exchange between intracellular and extracellular space
label: Abstract · what is new

stem: Which direction of influence between ion concentrations and neuroelectric activity did the in vitro experiments confirm?
choices: Fast activity modulates slow ion concentrations
The two fluctuate independently of each other
Slow ion concentrations modulate fast activity
Fast activity entrains ion concentrations one-to-one
answer: Slow ion concentrations modulate fast activity
label: Abstract · slow-fast relation

stem: Which three compartments does the underlying single-neuron model exchange ions between?
choices: Intracellular space, extracellular space, external bath
Soma, dendrite and extracellular space
Intracellular space, synaptic cleft and glial syncytium
Intracellular space, extracellular space and vasculature
answer: Intracellular space, extracellular space, external bath
label: Results · compartments

stem: Which activity pattern, alongside bursting and tonic spiking, did the decoupled single-neuron equations already produce?
choices: Spike frequency adaptation
Depolarization block
Subthreshold resonance
Spike-timing-dependent potentiation
answer: Depolarization block
label: Results · single-neuron repertoire

stem: Which variables make up the slow compartment of the single-neuron dynamics?
choices: The membrane potential
The potassium gating variable
The ion concentrations
The synaptic conductances
answer: The ion concentrations
label: Results · fast and slow

stem: Which parameter is tuned to make the modelled population excitatory rather than inhibitory?
choices: The maximal potassium conductance
The membrane capacitance
The synaptic reversal potential
The gating time constant
answer: The synaptic reversal potential
label: Results · excitation vs inhibition

stem: What shape does this model's membrane potential equation take, blocking the exact mean-field reduction that needs a quadratic one?
choices: A cubic-like function
A sigmoidal function
A piecewise linear function
An exponential function
answer: A cubic-like function
label: Results · why it is not exact

stem: How did the authors approximate the cubic-like membrane potential profile to proceed with the reduction?
choices: As two parabolas of opposite curvature joined stepwise
As a single parabola fitted by least squares
As a cubic expanded to first order about rest
As two straight lines joined at threshold
answer: As two parabolas of opposite curvature joined stepwise
label: Results · first approximation

stem: Under what population condition is the Lorentzian membrane-potential assumption a good approximation?
choices: When neurons fire fully asynchronously
When neurons operate close to synchrony
When the population splits above and below threshold
When excitability is homogeneous across neurons
answer: When neurons operate close to synchrony
label: Results · when Lorentzian holds

stem: What physiological argument justifies treating potassium concentrations as shared across the whole population?
choices: Astrocytes clamp potassium to a fixed value
Each neuron's own buffering dominates its environment
Potassium changes too slowly to differ between neurons
Diffusion equilibrates ions almost instantly at that scale
answer: Diffusion equilibrates ions almost instantly at that scale
label: Results · shared ion pool

stem: How is the gating variable governing potassium conductance handled in the mean-field derivation?
choices: As one population-averaged variable
As an independent variable per neuron
As a fixed constant through the simulation
As a function of the extracellular bath concentration
answer: As one population-averaged variable
label: Results · gating variable

stem: How many coupled equations does the mean-field model need, against four per neuron for the 3000-neuron network?
choices: Twelve equations
Five equations
Four equations
Forty equations
answer: Five equations
label: Results · dimensional saving

stem: How closely did the mean-field membrane potential track the average membrane potential of the 3000-neuron network?
choices: Qualitatively, not one-to-one
Exactly, within numerical error
Only in the depolarization block regime
Not at all outside tonic spiking
answer: Qualitatively, not one-to-one
label: Results · mean-field vs network

stem: What did network interaction do to burst frequency relative to the isolated single neuron?
choices: Slowed it down several fold
Left it unchanged
Sped it up several fold
Abolished bursting altogether
answer: Sped it up several fold
label: Results · frequency shift

stem: How was the effective external potassium concentration that aligns the mean-field with the population chosen?
choices: By least-squares fitting to the population traces
By analytic derivation from the coupling strength
By visual inspection of the match to the population
By matching the bifurcation diagrams of the two models
answer: By visual inspection of the match to the population
label: Results · effective bath value

stem: Which modelling difference did the authors blame for part of the mismatch between mean-field and network?
choices: The finite size of the simulated network
The use of all-to-all rather than random connectivity
The gating variable being shared in one and per-neuron in the other
The different integration time steps of the two models
answer: The gating variable being shared in one and per-neuron in the other
label: Results · source of mismatch

stem: Why can the in vitro traces not show the slow membrane potential shifts the model predicts?
choices: The electrodes sample too few neurons
The recordings are AC-coupled, filtering slow components
The slow shifts are masked by the potassium electrode
The bursts occur faster than the sampling rate
answer: The recordings are AC-coupled, filtering slow components
label: Results · what the LFP omits

stem: What joint pattern did both the neural mass model and the in vitro recordings show?
choices: Slow periodic potassium swings with bursts riding on them
Fast potassium swings with slow voltage drift
Steady potassium with periodic voltage bursts
Periodic potassium with no voltage bursts
answer: Slow periodic potassium swings with bursts riding on them
label: Results · the validated pattern

stem: Which in vitro observation did the authors say their deterministic model fails to reproduce?
choices: Bursts appearing without any potassium change
Potassium fluctuations without any bursts
Burst frequency slowing progressively over time
Bursts synchronizing across distant slices
answer: Burst frequency slowing progressively over time
label: Results · unexplained in vitro feature

stem: What regime did the mean-field model produce that the single-neuron model never showed?
choices: Isolated bursts within the up state
Depolarization block at low bath potassium
Tonic spiking with no potassium fluctuation
Complete silence at high bath potassium
answer: Isolated bursts within the up state
label: Results · emergent regime

stem: How was the fast subsystem defined for the multiple-timescale bifurcation analysis?
choices: Slow variables frozen and treated as parameters
Fast variables averaged over one burst cycle
Slow variables replaced by their time derivatives
Coupling set to zero to decouple the population
answer: Slow variables frozen and treated as parameters
label: Results · fast subsystem

stem: Which bifurcation curves bound the region where the fast subsystem oscillates?
choices: Saddle-node, pitchfork and transcritical
Saddle-homoclinic, Hopf and fold of limit cycles
Bogdanov-Takens, cusp and swallowtail
Period-doubling, torus and homoclinic tangency
answer: Saddle-homoclinic, Hopf and fold of limit cycles
label: Results · oscillatory region

stem: Near which codimension-two point are the single-neuron and neural mass models locally topologically equivalent?
choices: The Bogdanov-Takens point
The Hopf bifurcation point
The saddle-node-loop point
The fold of limit cycles point
answer: The saddle-node-loop point
label: Results · where the models agree

stem: What kind of transition generates seizure-like events in both the single-neuron and the neural mass model?
choices: Transitions between two coexisting limit cycles
A period-doubling cascade into chaos
A sudden change in the coupling strength
Transitions between fixed point and limit cycle
answer: Transitions between fixed point and limit cycle
label: Results · seizure mechanism

stem: What happens to the correspondence between single-neuron and neural mass dynamics away from the saddle-node-loop point?
choices: It holds throughout the parameter space
It breaks, and the mass model is simpler
It holds but with a constant frequency offset
It breaks, and the mass model is richer
answer: It breaks, and the mass model is richer
label: Results · where they diverge

stem: How was the proof-of-concept brain network simulation set up?
choices: Six identically weighted nodes, all tuned pathological
Six randomly weighted nodes, one tuned pathological
Two nodes coupled reciprocally, one pathological
Six nodes on an empirical human connectome
answer: Six randomly weighted nodes, one tuned pathological
label: Results · network demo

stem: What happened to the other nodes when global coupling was raised from zero to a high value?
choices: They suppressed the pathological node's bursts
They continued unaffected in a healthy regime
They burst only when their own bath value was raised
The pathological bursts spread to all of them
answer: The pathological bursts spread to all of them
label: Results · seizure spread

stem: Why did the authors attribute the downstream bursting to network re-organization rather than local pathology?
choices: Those regions received no structural connections
Their bath potassium was raised along with node D's
Their bursts preceded node D's in time
Those regions' local parameters were never changed
answer: Those regions' local parameters were never changed
label: Results · why nodes burst

stem: How thoroughly did the authors explore connectivity realizations and coupling strengths for the network demonstration?
choices: Systematically, across many realizations and strengths
Not at all; a single realization with no checks
Systematically for coupling, but one connectivity
Not systematically; one realization, with robustness observed
answer: Not systematically; one realization, with robustness observed
label: Results · how robust

stem: To what activity regime do the model's approximations restrict its validity?
choices: Fully asynchronous populations
Quasi-synchronous populations
Populations in depolarization block
Populations with homogeneous excitability
answer: Quasi-synchronous populations
label: Limitations · regime of validity

stem: What change to the spiking network would have narrowed its gap with the mean-field, and why did the authors not make it?
choices: Using more neurons, but the simulation cost was too high
Using random connectivity, but the derivation assumes all-to-all
Adding noise, but the model is deterministic
Sharing one gating variable, but the per-neuron version is more natural
answer: Sharing one gating variable, but the per-neuron version is more natural
label: Limitations · a fairer comparison

stem: Under what condition do the mean-field equations correspond one-to-one with the network simulations?
choices: When the coupling strength is small
When the membrane potential distribution is Lorentzian
When the bath potassium is in the healthy range
When the network size exceeds three thousand neurons
answer: When the membrane potential distribution is Lorentzian
label: Limitations · when they match

stem: Which extension did the authors propose for the regimes their Lorentzian assumption fails in?
choices: A Gaussian distribution of membrane potentials
A bimodal, double-Lorentzian distribution
A second slow variable for sodium
A stochastic forcing term on the bath concentration
answer: A bimodal, double-Lorentzian distribution
label: Limitations · proposed extension

stem: What did the authors hold constant in the two-parabola approximation that could instead vary?
choices: The bath potassium concentration
The parabola coefficients
The synaptic coupling strength
The excitability distribution width
answer: The parabola coefficients
label: Limitations · fixed coefficients

stem: What approximation defines the firing rate in the thermodynamic limit of this model?
choices: A fixed threshold at the resting potential
A heterogeneous threshold drawn per neuron
A firing threshold taken to infinity
A threshold set by the bath concentration
answer: A firing threshold taken to infinity
label: Limitations · firing rate definition

stem: Which two facts did the authors give for the correspondence with networks and experiments being qualitative only?
choices: Finite network size and connectivity that is not all-to-all
Measurement noise and limited recording duration
Parameter uncertainty and integration error
Species differences and temperature differences
answer: Finite network size and connectivity that is not all-to-all
label: Limitations · not quantitative

stem: Which cell population's influence on excitability does the bath potassium parameter let this model begin to represent?
choices: Inhibitory interneurons
Thalamic relay neurons
Glia
Endothelial cells of the vasculature
answer: Glia
label: Limitations · glial role
